headline: Oil near US$115, a Bank of Canada hike and tariff pressure dominate the week
summary: The Iran war kept oil above US$110, pushing the Bank of Canada to raise its rate to 2.50% on Wednesday. Ottawa faces new 50% U.S. tariffs on Oct. 30, GTA voters picked new mayors, and the U.S. midterms and Israel's election add uncertainty.

top.headline: Oil near US$115 as Iran war talks stall and Houthis hit Saudi sites
top.what: The Qatari draft deal drew an 'unacceptable' response from Tehran while Brent stayed above US$110 and the Houthis claimed a strike on Ras Tanura.
top.why: It keeps Ontario gas and diesel prices high and feeds inflation.

top.headline: Bank of Canada hikes to 2.50%, its first increase since 2023
top.what: Inflation hit 3.1% in September on gasoline prices, and the bank raised its rate a quarter point on Wednesday, signalling more could follow.
top.why: Variable-rate mortgages and credit lines get costlier.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade fight deepens ahead of new 50% tariffs on Oct. 30
top.what: A reported U.S. envoy warning and fresh tariffs on consumer goods keep pressure on Ottawa before the midterms.
top.why: Tariffs hit Ontario manufacturers and consumer prices.

top.headline: Chow re-elected; GTA voters oust mayors in Mississauga, Hamilton, Oakville
top.what: Toronto's mayor won a second term while several GTA cities chose new mayors.
top.why: New councils will set housing, transit and tax priorities.

top.headline: Midterms near as Trump campaigns in Ohio and early voting surges
top.what: Control of Congress is at stake on Nov. 3, with Texas early voting above 20%.
top.why: The result shapes U.S. trade and Iran policy that affects Canada.

top.headline: Israel's election leaves Netanyahu's bloc short of a majority
top.what: Counting shows Netanyahu's bloc at 54 seats and Eisenkot's at 49, with coalition talks to follow.
top.why: The outcome affects Middle East diplomacy and oil markets.

top.headline: Ottawa presses Stelco owner over Hamilton job cuts
top.what: Minister Joly won't meet the owner's CEO without a plan to restore jobs.
top.why: Steel jobs in Hamilton and the wider region are at risk.

top.headline: Fed expected to hold as AI-stock jitters hit markets
top.what: Investors await the Fed decision and Microsoft and Alphabet results.
top.why: Moves in U.S. markets and rates spill into Canadian borrowing costs and pensions.
